summary: Iteration 5 focused testing — cross-router push integration (send_to_user helper called from routers/admin.py verify_payment and routers/payments.py _apply_midtrans_update). All 7 review criteria PASS. New test file test_push_integration.py: 13/13 pass. Full regression: 76/84 pass (same 8 pre-existing Karimunjawa featured_trip[0] seat-exhaustion failures from iter 1-4, ZERO new regressions from send_to_user integration). Key verifications: (1) Backend starts clean — no circular import between routers/admin.py, routers/payments.py, routers/push.py; send_to_user is the SAME object imported in all three. (2) POST /api/admin/bookings/{id}/verify with status='verified' returns exactly {ok:true}, booking transitions payment_status→'verified' + booking_status→'confirmed'. (3) POST /api/admin/bookings/{id}/verify with status='rejected' returns {ok:true}, booking→cancelled AND booked_seats decremented back by exact quantity (verified with pre/post snapshot on trip 6a5d8a13a301cc285bad3474). (4) send_to_user() invoked ASYNC directly with (a) nonexistent user_id, (b) empty string, (c) None → all return 0, never raise. (5) Midtrans webhook: invalid signature → 401 'Invalid signature'; valid SHA512 signature but unknown order_id → 200 {ok:true, note:...} (does not crash). (6) Full E2E: traveler subscribed a fake FCM endpoint via /api/push/subscribe, admin verified their booking → verify returned {ok:true}, backend logs show 'Push failed for https://fcm.googleapis.com/fcm/send/TEST_ITER5_… WebPushException: Invalid p256dh key specified' (as expected — fire-and-forget swallows the failure, does not propagate to HTTP response). (7) verify_payment refactor (reading booking BEFORE update instead of only inside rejected branch) preserved rejected-path seat-release behavior exactly. send_to_user is truly fire-and-forget: even with real HTTP attempt to fake endpoint, admin/verify contract stays {ok:true}. VAPID keys are configured (enabled=true in /api/push/config).

minor.issue: PRE-EXISTING (not iter 5) — passing invalid booking_id string (e.g. literal 'None') raises bson.errors.InvalidId → 500 instead of 400/404. Reproduced in backend logs during cascade of Karimunjawa-seat-exhaustion failures. Suggest wrapping ObjectId(booking_id) in try/except → HTTPException(404). Same pattern already used correctly in payments.py create_snap_token/status.

NOT caused by iter 5 push integration (iter 5 tests bypass featured[0] via _find_bookable_trip helper and pass 100%). Fix: reset booked_seats on Karimunjawa in seed OR change TestBookingsFlow to use a trip with capacity.

action_items: OPTIONAL — reset booked_seats on Karimunjawa featured trip (or use a different index in TestBookingsFlow) to unblock the 8 pre-existing regression failures. NOT related to iteration 5 push work.
OPTIONAL (defensive) — wrap ObjectId(booking_id) in /api/admin/bookings/{id}/verify in try/except to return 404 instead of 500 on invalid IDs. Same pattern as routers/payments.py.
critical_code_review_comments: GOOD: routers/push.py send_to_user() is textbook fire-and-forget — early-returns 0 when VAPID_PRIVATE unset OR user_id falsy; wraps entire body in try/except returning 0 on any error; auto-cleans dead subs via delete_many. Cannot raise → cannot break the caller's HTTP contract.

GOOD: routers/admin.py verify_payment refactor — now reads `b = await db.bookings.find_one(...)` BEFORE any conditional branching (line 83). Same seat-release behavior for rejected path (line 88-92). Push notification block (line 95-105) is guarded by `if b:` so a missing booking still returns {ok:true} without crash.

GOOD: routers/payments.py _apply_midtrans_update wraps push call in the payment_status transition guard (`if prev.get('payment_status') != payment_status:` line 69) → prevents duplicate notifications on webhook retries. Excellent idempotency.

GOOD: No circular import — routers/push.py imports only db + security; routers/admin.py + routers/payments.py both import `from routers.push import send_to_user` after their own imports. Verified: same function object identity across all three modules.

MINOR: In routers/admin.py verify_payment, if payment.status='rejected' AND booking has non-ObjectId trip_id, the ObjectId(b['trip_id']) on line 90 could raise InvalidId 500. Unlikely in practice but not defensively guarded. Same MINOR pre-existing concern with booking_id path param → wrap in try/except.
